Exercise A

A Story of Change

Read the text and fill in each gap with the correct word.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading text

Australia's history with its First Nations peoples is long and painful — but it is also a story of change. For more than 1 years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples cared for the land.

After 2, when the British arrived, that land was taken from them, and for many years they were not counted as citizens in their own country. Until 1967, the constitution did not even 3 Aboriginal people. Then, in a historic referendum, more than 90 per cent of Australians voted 4 to change that. Aboriginal people were finally given a voice in the nation's laws.

Slowly, more changed. In 1992, the High Court recognised 5 title in the famous Mabo decision, and land rights were returned to the Meriam people of the Torres Strait. In 2008, the 6 said sorry to the Stolen Generations — Aboriginal children who had been 7 from their families. The apology was watched by thousands of people around the country.

Today, Aboriginal culture 8 in art, music and festivals. But the work is not finished: many people say that real respect must be shown in health, education and jobs.

Exercise B

The Right Passive

Choose the correct passive form. Remember: most verbs with two objects can form two passives — "She was told the news" or "The news was told to her".

Australia then and now

1. In 1962, Aboriginal people the right to vote in federal elections.

2. In the Mabo decision, their land back to the Meriam people.

3. The Stolen Generations a formal apology in 2008.

4. At the cultural centre, visitors the story of the Dreamtime.

5. At many mission schools, Aboriginal children English, not their own languages.

6. Free park maps to every visitor at the gate.

7. By the time the British arrived, Aboriginal people for the land for thousands of years.

8. The didgeridoo at the concert last night.

Exercise C

Turn It Round

Rewrite each active sentence in the passive. Start with the person or thing in bold. Be careful with the verb form!

Your turn
Verbs with two objects you will need: give hand back offer show teach tell

1. The government gave Aboriginal people the right to vote in 1962.
→

2. The High Court handed the Meriam people back their land in 1992.
→

3. In 2008, the prime minister offered the Stolen Generations a formal apology.
→

4. The guide shows visitors sacred rock paintings.
→

5. The teachers taught the children English at the mission school.
→

6. Next year, the council will give young artists a grant for their paintings.
→

7. Yesterday, an elder told us the story of the Rainbow Serpent.
→

Exercise D

Writing: A Moment of Change

Your Australian exchange partner's class is preparing a poster exhibition about Indigenous Australian history for the school open day. Write a short poster text (6–8 sentences) about one moment of change: the 1967 referendum, the 1992 Mabo decision or the 2008 apology. Use at least four passive sentences, including two with two objects.

Useful phrases
You can use these: In 19…, Aboriginal people were given … … was handed back to … … were offered … Visitors are shown … Today, … is celebrated …
Your poster text
Aim for 6–8 sentences: 4+ passive sentences, 2 of them with two objects.
